title: Word RAM acceptance implies nondeterministic log space
statement: Let $P$ be an extended Word RAM program, let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings, and let $c,F_0\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every input $x$ there is a time bound $t$ such that, for every coin string $\rho$, the program halts within $t$ steps using words of width $c(\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+1)$ and at most $F_0$ touched memory addresses, with some output. Suppose also that $x\in L$ exactly when there are coin and output strings for which it halts within that time and space bound with acceptance. Then $L$ is decidable in nondeterministic space $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$.
